steps.text: NA-0763 (D-0040; spine D-1404) -- THE LIVENESS TICK. Instruments I1-I5 per the Director's ruling R8. The app runs under the TEST-ONLY tempo seam QSLD_TICK_MS, which gui_driver.rs injects into the child environment the same way runner.py already injects QSLD_DATA_DIR. The seam rides app_info -- a Serialize-only DTO with no save path -- so no code path can round-trip a test tempo into settings.json (ruling R4).

⚠⚠ FAIL FAST IF THE TEMPO SEAM IS ABSENT. This scenario is meaningless without `QSLD_TICK_MS`: at the shipped INSTANT tempo a beat is 15-25 s, so I1's bounded window sees ~1 tick and the run fails with a confusing `I1_tick_fires TIMEOUT, last=1` that looks like a product defect. It is not -- it means the scenario was invoked WITHOUT its seam (running `runner.py` directly rather than through `gui_driver.rs`, which sets it). Measured the hard way, twice. Assert it up front so the failure names its own cause.
A vault, so the run reaches an unlocked surface. The tick is gated on exactly the two post-unlock screens, the same gate the idle autolock uses.

I2, FIRST HALF -- the gate is CLOSED on a fresh profile because NO RELAY is configured (ruling R10: unlocked AND a relay configured). This also proves the arm is not vacuous: the gate is observably closed BEFORE it is observably opened.

Configure a relay through the app's own IPC. relay_config_set normalizes and saves; it requires no probe, so no network is touched. The address is deliberately UNREACHABLE -- nothing in this scenario needs it to answer, and a reachable one would make the run depend on a relay.

⚠ THE TWO IPC CALLS ARE SPLIT AND EACH CAPTURES ITS OWN REJECTION. The first version chained them with no .catch(), so a rejection anywhere left one boolean reading false forever and the row could only say 'last=false' -- which is exactly what it said when this failed on CI while passing locally. An instrument that cannot name its own failure is not an instrument.

steps.script: window.__na0763 = { setDone:false, mainDone:false, err:null }; invoke("relay_config_set", { url: "https://relay.invalid.example" })   .then(function(){ window.__na0763.setDone = true; })   .catch(function(e){ window.__na0763.err = "relay_config_set: " + String((e && e.message) || e); }); return "kicked";

steps.text: Now the surface re-read that publishes the relay into the tick's gate. Kept as a REAL call to `enterMain` rather than assigning the flag directly: assigning it would bypass the very wiring under test (R10's gate is fed by enterMain and refreshServerState, not by the scenario).

steps.script: window.__na0763.err = null; enterMain()   .then(function(){ window.__na0763.mainDone = true; })   .catch(function(e){ window.__na0763.err = "enterMain: " + String((e && e.message) || e); }); return "kicked";

steps.text: I1 TICK-FIRES -- with the seam shortened, at least TWO handler runs carrying source=tick inside a BOUNDED window. This is a bounded poll that FAILS on timeout, never a sleep: a tick that never fires produces a red row. RED ARM: disable the timer and this cannot pass.

I4 + R6 -- THE MARKER SEPARATION, WHICH IS THE WHOLE REASON THE TWO COMMITTED why:surface_open ASSERTIONS SURVIVE. redeemMark is a single-slot last-write-wins surface. Ticks have now fired repeatedly; the slot must STILL read the last USER-caused trigger (unlock), never 'tick'. If the tick ever writes that slot, this row goes red HERE and f_l_invite_redeem's two expects go red there.

I3 SINGLE-FLIGHT -- a trigger arriving mid-scan must NOT start a second scan; it sets the pending slot and never stacks. ⚠ THE TICK'S OWN GATE IS CLOSED FOR THIS WINDOW so the only scans in flight are the two this step issues -- otherwise the counters are contaminated by the very timer under test. Measured live before that was done: the running tick was refused 60 times in one window, which is the guard working, but it is not a DETERMINISTIC arm.

steps.script: window.__na0763.savedRelay = tickRelayConfigured; tickRelayConfigured = false; return String(tickGateOpen());

steps.text: ⚠ WAIT FOR QUIESCENCE BEFORE MEASURING, rather than assuming it. Closing the gate stops NEW beats; it does not abort a scan already in flight. Measured the hard way: without this the delta read 2, because a tick's scan was still running and BOTH calls below were refused.

steps.script: window.__na0763.rej0 = relayScanBusyRejects; window.__na0763.rer0 = relayScanRerunCount; relayScan({ source:"unlock", at: Date.now() }); relayScan({ source:"surface_open", at: Date.now() }); return String(relayScanBusyRejects - window.__na0763.rej0);

steps.text: The refusal above is read in the SAME synchronous turn as the two calls, so nothing can interleave: JS is single-threaded and `relayScan` runs to its first await before returning. That is what makes 'exactly one' a fact rather than a race.
And the pending slot is EMPTY afterwards -- the rerun consumed it, and a second trigger did not queue a second one behind it.
Restore the tick's gate; the remaining arms need it live.

I5 BACKOFF-REPORT, and its bound is stated rather than glossed (ruling R8). The RELAY-FAULT path to this state is NOT drivable here: a fresh profile has no pending contact, so no relay call is ever attempted and no failure can accrue. What IS driven is the half this lane owns -- the threshold, the surface and the recovery -- through the handler's own outcome recorder. The unreachable-relay PATH is FIELD-VERIFIED on the acceptance flight.

steps.script: for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++) {   recordScanOutcome({ source:"tick", at: Date.now() },     { why:"tick", scanned:1, finished:0, pending:1, attempted:1, failed:1 }); } return String(tickFails);

steps.text: NA-0779 (18c L6): the outage now reads 'Relay: unreachable' in the bar's left span; recovery -- one scan that reaches the relay -- flips relayProven and reads 'Relay: connected' (F3: a measured success). The bar's class carries status-bar beside status-line.

NA-0764 (R5) RE-AIM, WITH ITS OWN CAN-FAIL PROOF. These three rows moved from #tick-status to #status-line because F1 migrated the message into the footer's closed reason set. A re-aimed assertion is a DIFFERENT assertion, so the row below first proves the quiet line is now SILENT -- if the message were still there, the re-aim would be additive rather than a migration and this row would fail.

steps.expect: Relay: unreachable · Vault: unlocked · Auto-lock: 60 min

steps.text: RECOVERY CLEARS IT -- one scan that reaches the relay and does not fail resets the counter and hides the line. A status that appears and never leaves is its own defect.

steps.script: recordScanOutcome({ source:"tick", at: Date.now() },   { why:"tick", scanned:1, finished:0, pending:1, attempted:1, failed:0 }); return String(tickFails);

steps.text: RECOVERY IS A SIMPLE RETURN TO NORMAL -- no 'Reconnected' blurb, refused for this lane (ruling R5). The trouble CLASS is gone and the line answers Ready again, which is the whole of the recovery behaviour.

I2 SECOND HALF -- LOCKED ACROSS THE WINDOW => ZERO TICK SCANS. The count is sampled at the lock, a BOUNDED window of real elapsed time is then measured on the page's own clock (many seam-beats' worth of opportunity), and the delta must be EXACTLY zero.

steps.script: window.__na0763.locked = false; invoke("lock_now").then(function(){ return showUnlockScreen("main"); })   .then(function(){ window.__na0763.locked = true; })   .catch(function(e){ window.__na0763.err = "lock: " + String((e && e.message) || e); }); return "kicked";

steps.text: ⚠ THE LOCKED WINDOW STARTS **HERE**, not when the lock was REQUESTED. Measured the hard way: at an adversarial 30 ms seam this arm read a delta of 2, because ~2 beats fit between asking to lock and the screen actually changing -- and those ticks are CORRECT, the vault was not locked yet. Sampling after `scr-unlock` is visible makes the arm measure what it claims to measure, at any tempo.

steps.script: window.__na0763.atLock = tickCount; window.__na0763.lockedAt = Date.now(); return String(tickGateOpen());

steps.text: And the schedule RESET rather than merely paused: a due-time computed before the lock must not survive it, or the first pass after an unlock would fire immediately.
